issues.t: Timing chain guides wear and break
issues.sym: A whine or rattle from the front of the engine, loudest on a cold start or when revving. It can progress to misfires, a check engine light, a stall or an engine that will not start.
issues.why: The first N20 engines used plastic timing chain guides that turn brittle and break. Loose pieces fall into the oil pan, the chain gets slack and can jump a tooth or snap, which can wreck the engine. BMW changed the parts in early 2015.
issues.next: Do not ignore a new whine or rattle. Have a BMW specialist inspect the chain soon, and ask about any remaining extended coverage from the class-action settlement. Replacing the chain before it fails is far cheaper than a new engine.

issues.t: Coolant leaks and electric water pump failure
issues.sym: Low coolant warnings, puddles or a sweet smell under the hood, the temperature gauge climbing, or a sudden overheating warning with reduced power.
issues.why: Many cooling parts are plastic: the water pump housing, thermostat housing, expansion tank, hoses and radiator ends. They crack with age and heat. The electric water pump can also quit with little warning.
issues.next: If the overheating warning comes on, pull over and shut the engine off. Have the cooling system pressure-tested to find the leak; replacing the failed part early avoids head gasket damage.

issues.t: Oil leaks from the valve cover and oil filter housing
issues.sym: Burning oil smell, light smoke from the engine bay, oil spots under the car, or the oil level dropping between changes.
issues.why: The plastic valve cover and its rubber gasket, and the oil filter housing gasket, harden and crack from years of heat cycles. Oil then drips onto the hot exhaust. Newer engines have fewer reports, but filter housing and crankcase vent leaks still show up.
issues.next: Have the leak traced to its source. Fix it soon, since oil on the exhaust is a fire risk and oil on belts and engine mounts damages them.

issues.t: Coolant pump connector can short and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Often no warning. Some owners see a coolant temperature or water pump warning, or smell burning plastic from the engine bay.
issues.why: The electrical connector on the electric coolant pump may not seal out water. Moisture can short the connector and start a fire, even with the car parked.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-608 and book the free dealer repair. Until then, park outside and away from buildings if you can.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can rupture (recalls)
issues.sym: No symptoms before a crash.
issues.why: The driver frontal airbag inflator, including some interim replacement inflators, can degrade with heat and humidity and burst in a crash, throwing metal fragments.
issues.next: Run your VIN through the recall lookup. If recall 16V-071, 19V-016 or 20V-017 is open, get the free airbag replacement right away.

issues.t: Brake vacuum pump can fail and stiffen the pedal (recalls)
issues.sym: The brake pedal suddenly feels hard and you need much more force to stop. A brake warning may appear.
issues.why: The engine-driven brake vacuum pump may not get enough oil, so it wears out and stops making the vacuum that powers the brake booster.
issues.next: Check for recalls 13V-454 and 14V-627 and have the free dealer repair done. If the pedal goes hard, press firmly and get the car checked before driving further.

issues.t: Battery cable connection can overheat and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving and may not restart. Electrical systems can cut out.
issues.why: The main positive battery cable connection at the fuse box can develop high resistance and lose power.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 17V-087 and have the free connector replacement done.

issues.t: Rattles and squeaks from the dashboard and trim
issues.sym: Rattling, buzzing or squeaking from the dashboard, doors or rear of the car, especially on rough roads.
issues.why: Loose or rubbing interior trim panels and clips. Owners report it as one of the most common complaints on this generation.
issues.next: Note exactly where and when it happens and have the dealer or a trim shop pad or re-clip the panel.

issues.t: Cracked engine mounts
issues.sym: Clunking or thumping from the front when shifting or pulling away, extra vibration at idle, and the engine shaking more than it should.
issues.why: The engine mounts, usually the upper passenger-side mount first, crack or wear out. Some fail before 20,000 miles; most go by around 100,000.
issues.next: Have the mounts inspected if the car shakes or clunks. A failed mount is not an emergency, but leaving it lets the engine move and strains hoses and other mounts.

issues.t: Rough idle or stalling after a cold start
issues.sym: The engine idles roughly or the rpm bounces after a cold start. It may sputter, shake or stall when you shift into gear.
issues.why: An engine software issue on early second-generation cars. BMW released a bulletin in late 2017 with an engine computer software update.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check whether the latest engine software is installed. Letting the engine idle a little longer before shifting is a short-term workaround.

issues.t: Front control arm clunk over bumps
issues.sym: A clunk or crunching noise from the front, often the passenger side, when going over speed bumps or potholes.
issues.why: The front lower control arms (wishbones) on early cars can develop play. BMW issued a 2016 bulletin to replace both with an updated part.
issues.next: Have the front suspension checked and ask the dealer about the bulletin and updated control arms.

issues.t: Transmission message asks you to use the parking brake
issues.sym: A random warning when parking says to secure the car with the parking brake and see a service center. The car may not seem to go into Park properly.
issues.why: A small spring in the gear selector's shift-lock solenoid does not engage reliably, so the car cannot confirm it is in Park.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake until it is fixed. Ask a shop whether the selector spring can be repaired before paying for a whole new gear selector.

issues.t: Brake pads and rotors wear out quickly
issues.sym: Brake wear warnings or squealing as soon as about 20,000 miles, and frequent pad changes front and rear.
issues.why: Pad compounds chosen for strong braking, plus the stability control system applying the brakes, wear pads and rotors faster than on many other small SUVs.
issues.next: Budget for brake service more often than usual. Rear pad changes need a scan tool to retract the electronic parking brake.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may be blocked by the dashboard (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms before a crash.
issues.why: The instrument panel may stop the front passenger airbag from opening the way it should.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 17V-062 and get the free dealer repair.

issues.t: Driver seat belt may not lock (recall)
issues.sym: No obvious symptom in daily driving.
issues.why: The locking mechanism in the driver's seat belt retractor may not lock as designed in a crash or hard stop.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 16V-747 and have the free repair done.

issues.t: Seat side airbags may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptom; an airbag warning light may come on.
issues.why: The igniters for the seat-mounted side airbags may fail to fire, so the side airbag would not inflate in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 16V-914 and have the free repair done.

issues.t: B-pillar trim may not cushion a head impact (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms in daily driving.
issues.why: The upper trim on the pillar between the front and rear doors may not absorb enough energy if an occupant's head hits it in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 19V-349 and have the free trim replacement done.

issues.t: Crankshaft sensor software can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine can shut off while driving, and may restart only after a short wait.
issues.why: The crankshaft position sensor was built with incorrect software, which can cause the engine to stall.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 18V-465 and have the free sensor replacement done.

issues.t: Tie rods may wear and break (recall)
issues.sym: Steering feels loose or wanders, a clunk from the front, or in the worst case a loss of steering control.
issues.why: Some tie rods were assembled incorrectly and can wear and break.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 19V-601. Get it repaired right away, and stop driving if the steering feels loose.

issues.t: Taillight mounts can crack and loosen (recall)
issues.sym: A taillight that sits loose, moves, or falls out.
issues.why: The plastic brackets that hold the taillight housing can crack.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 19V-074 and have the free repair done.

issues.t: Rollover sensor fault can stop airbags firing (recall)
issues.sym: An airbag warning light may come on.
issues.why: A fault in the rollover sensor inside the airbag control unit may keep the head airbags and seat belt pretensioners from firing in a rollover.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 20V-283 and have the free control unit replacement done.

issues.t: Passenger seat belt retractor may release too early (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms in daily driving.
issues.why: The front passenger seat belt retractor can switch off its force limiting too soon in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 21V-554 and have the free inspection and repair done.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel rail can crack and leak fuel (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell, especially near the engine, or a check engine light.
issues.why: The high-pressure fuel rail may crack and leak gasoline onto the engine, which can start a fire.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, stop driving and have it towed. Check your VIN for recall 22V-513 and get the free fuel rail replacement.

issues.t: Driver front airbag may not deploy properly (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms before a crash.
issues.why: Some driver airbags were built incorrectly and may not inflate as intended.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V-079 and have the free airbag replacement done.

issues.t: Rear seat belts can be pinched by trim (recall)
issues.sym: A rear outer seat belt that is hard to pull out or does not retract smoothly.
issues.why: An interior trim panel can pinch the second-row outer seat belts, which were trapped during assembly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V-260 and have the free trim adjustment done.

issues.t: Integrated brake system can lose power assist (recalls)
issues.sym: Brake and stability control warnings, a hard brake pedal, and longer stopping distances. ABS and stability control may stop working.
issues.why: The integrated brake unit, which combines the brake booster with ABS and stability control, can malfunction. BMW has issued several campaigns, and earlier repairs may need a newer fix.
issues.next: If brake warnings come on, drive gently to a dealer or have it towed. Check your VIN for recalls 24V-104, 24V-739 and 26V-422.

issues.t: Brake module motor welds can break (recall)
issues.sym: Brake warning lights, reduced brake assist, and ABS or stability control turning off. Rear brakes may not apply as they should.
issues.why: Welds inside the servomotor of the integrated brake control module may break.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-697 and have the free module replacement done.

issues.t: Hesitation when pulling away from a stop
issues.sym: After you press the gas from a stop or rolling stop, the car pauses for a second or two and then surges. On a slight slope it may roll before Drive or Reverse engages. Downshifts can lag after hard acceleration.
issues.why: Owners trace it to how the dual-clutch transmission and engine software manage launch. Dealer software updates have not cured it for everyone.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check for transmission and engine software updates and to document the complaint. Leave extra room when pulling into traffic.

issues.t: Infotainment screen freezes and CarPlay drops out
issues.sym: The center screen freezes or lags, the radio locks up until the system reboots, and Apple CarPlay disconnects or will not reconnect.
issues.why: Software glitches in the newer iDrive system.
issues.next: Ask the dealer for the latest iDrive software update. A system reboot (holding the volume knob) usually clears a freeze.

issues.t: B-pillar reinforcement plates may be too weak (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms in daily driving.
issues.why: Some reinforcement plates in the pillars between the doors may not be as strong as designed, which weakens side-crash protection.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-829 and have the free inspection done.

issues.t: Front seat belt retractors may not hold (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms in daily driving.
issues.why: A damaged torsion bar in the front seat belt retractors may not restrain the occupant properly in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-616 and have the free seat belt replacement done.
